query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Using a nickel-based alloy, specifically Inconel 625, for the preparation of parts for the dipping and plating equipment will protect the equipment from erosion and corrosion due to its high-temperature resistance and corrosion resistance properties.
generation.intervention: Exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum at 700°C for an extended period
generation.conditions: Immersion in liquid aluminum for 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer on the surface of the Inconel 625 alloy
generation.mechanism: The nickel-based alloy will form a stable and adherent oxide layer, which will prevent the penetration of liquid aluminum and reduce the corrosion rate
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in corrosion rate by at least 80% compared to common materials, with a maximum corrosion depth of 0.1 mm
generation.baseline: Common materials used in the industry, such as steel or aluminum alloys
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 600-800°C and exposure time of up to 200 hours
generation.uncertainty: The actual corrosion rate may vary depending on the specific composition of the Inconel 625 alloy and the exact conditions of the hot dip aluminum plating process

falsification_experiment.design: Immersion test in liquid aluminum at 700°C for 100 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion depth exceeds 0.2 mm or the corrosion rate is less than 60% reduction compared to common materials, the hypothesis is falsified
